- If sentiment is high (≥0.6) and forecast is rising sharply, reduce peak overshoot by 5–10% to avoid overreaction.
- If sentiment is low (≤0.4) and forecast is falling, avoid premature bottoming — delay downward correction by 1–2 periods.
- When true price rises >10% from recent 5-day average, model tends to overestimate — cap forecast increase at 80% of true rise.
- If sentiment swings sharply (e.g., from 0.9 to 0.1), model often misreads momentum — adjust forecast to mean-revert toward 3–5-day moving average.
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently overestimates late-period (last 7–10 days) prices — reduce forecast by 2–5% for final 10 days if sentiment is neutral or declining.
- If sentiment is consistently above 0.6 over 5+ days, model tends to overfit recent highs — apply downward bias of 3–5% to avoid “sentiment-driven inflation.”
